name: Suspension Trainer Dip
summary: A bodyweight pressing exercise performed using suspension straps that targets the triceps, chest, and anterior deltoids while challenging shoulder stability.

setup: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to roughly waist height.
Grasp both handles using a neutral grip, palms facing inward.
Press down into the handles to lock out your arms in a tall support position, with feet placed on the floor to regulate assistance as needed.
steps: Keep your chest proud and core tight as you bend your elbows to lower your body in a controlled descent.
Descend until your elbows reach approximately a 90-degree angle, keeping the handles close to your sides.
Drive your palms downward into the handles, extending your elbows to press back up to the top lockout.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower your body under control; exhale forcefully as you press back up to full extension.
cues: Keep the straps tight and hands pinned close to your ribs.
Maintain active, depressed shoulders without shrugging.
Control the handles to prevent them from drifting outward.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the hands and handles to drift wide away from the torso.
common_faults.correction: Actively pull the handles into your sides and engage the lats and chest to stabilize the straps.

common_faults.fault: Shoulders shrugging up toward the ears at the bottom.
common_faults.correction: Keep scapulae depressed by actively pushing down through the palms throughout the entire movement.

common_faults.fault: Excessive forward shoulder dump at depth.
common_faults.correction: Limit the depth to approximately 90 degrees at the elbows and keep your chest lifted.

precautions: Ensure the suspension anchor is completely secure before supporting bodyweight.
Use foot assistance on the floor if you cannot maintain stable shoulder alignment.
